Definition: {Babel (i.e. Babylon), including Babylonia and the Babylonian empire}
BiblicalUsage: Babel in Aramaic is the name of the city and empire in Daniel's day — the Babylon of Nebuchadnezzar's court, where Daniel served and where the king's wise men could not tell the dream. Daniel's God revealed what Babylon's gods could not, and the king's decrees went out from Babel to all the peoples of the empire.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Babel in Aramaic is the same Babel as in Hebrew, and the lesson is the same: the greatest empire on earth cannot read a dream, but Daniel's God can. That is why I trust him, not the empire.
